clue.text: Join two sailors in savings scheme for capital

parts.note: to join things on is to add them

indicators.note: the two sailors sit inside the savings scheme's letters

parts.note: an ISA is a UK tax-free Individual Savings Account
AB is an able-bodied seaman
the second AB for the second sailor

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put a pair of seamen into a savings plan to build up capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as money to save, but it is a capital city. ISA is a British tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia.

clue.text: Elbows out a Kipling character: lad not unknown

parts.note: Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel of that name

indicators.note: an unknown in algebra is y, so the word for lad drops that letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A Kipling figure is described as standing with elbows out, a boy who is no stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing with hands on hips and elbows bent outward is the posture described by this adverb.

clue.text: Diptera as distributed essentially unalike

indicators.note: letters spread about and laid out afresh signal a rearrangement of the fodder

explanation.surface: Flies of the order Diptera, spread around, turn out to be fundamentally different from one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as distributed' looks like a phrase, but 'as' is fodder and 'distributed' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are disparate are fundamentally different, not able to be compared.

clue.text: In post, cardinal with church given porridge

indicators.note: the number and the church go inside the word for post

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a cardinal number such as ten
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church cardinal is posted somewhere and handed a bowl of breakfast oats.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a prison term, so someone given porridge has been jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given porridge means receiving a prison term, which is being sentenced.

clue.text: Money needed for memorial

definitions.meaning: a monumental ... is an engraved plaque set in a church floor or wall to commemorate someone

explanation.surface: Cash is required to put up a memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is both slang for cash and an engraved commemorative plaque in a church.

clue.text: Poor cricket side hosting first-class game

indicators.note: the word for first-class is taken in by the other pieces, like a guest

parts.note: poor in quality means bad
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
in mint condition means first-class, as new

explanation.surface: A weak cricket team takes on a top-quality game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the on side (leg side) is the half of the field the batsman stands facing away from.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played with shuttlecocks over a net.

clue.text: Confused state reported in Mons for example?

indicators.note: something reported is spoken, so the word for a confused state is heard, not written

parts.note: to be in a daze is to be confused

explanation.surface: A state of confusion is said to have been recorded in the Belgian town of Mons.
explanation.walkthrough: Mons looks like the Belgian town; read it as plural of Mon, short for Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: Mon is the short form of Monday, so Mons are examples of weekdays.

clue.text: Sober group securing reduced payment for venue

indicators.note: the two letters of the sober group hold the shortened payment between them

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous

indicators.note: cut short, the word for payment loses its last letter

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for a home

explanation.surface: A group of teetotallers secures a cut-price fee for their meeting place.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place where events are held, a venue.

clue.text: Surprised Rosebud perhaps devouring pastry

indicators.note: one word eats another, so the pastry goes inside the toboggan

parts.note: Rosebud was the childhood sled in the film Citizen Kane
a tart is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: Someone called Rosebud, perhaps a pet, is caught by surprise while wolfing down a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosebud perhaps' is the famous sled from Citizen Kane, not a flower or a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To be startled is to be given a sudden fright or surprise.

clue.text: Lower-class alliance losing heart in revolution

indicators.note: turned right round, the remaining letters are read backwards
the middle letter of the alliance word is dropped

parts.note: a union is an alliance

explanation.surface: A workers' alliance gives up its spirit during an uprising of the lower orders.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is the old British label for speech or manners not used by the upper class. Losing heart leaves UNON; revolution turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U was coined for words and habits marking someone as not upper class.

clue.text: Author Edith briefly recalled dramatist

indicators.note: called back, the shortened surname is read in reverse
cut short, the surname loses its final letter

parts.note: Edith Nesbit wrote The Railway Children

explanation.surface: A children's writer, briefly remembered, recalls a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Briefly cuts NESBIT to NESBI; recalled turns that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Stories about theologian bored by Catholic Church stars

indicators.note: the collection of stories wraps round everything else

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings

indicators.note: the theologian's letters are drilled into by the Church

parts.note: DD is a Doctor of Divinity
Rome stands for the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: Tales are told about a divine whose life was pierced by the Catholic Church, with stars in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored by' puts the Church inside the theologian, and 'about' wraps the stories round that. Ana is an old word for a collection of anecdotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, and also a galaxy, made up of stars.

clue.text: Black water for the maker of The 14 Across of 6 Across

definitions.text: the maker of The 14 Across of 6 Across

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: Dark water is the work of the artist behind a famous picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ancient of Days is William Blake's 1794 picture of God measuring the world with dividers.
explanation.definitionFit: William Blake painted and engraved The Ancient of Days, the frontispiece to Europe a Prophecy.

clue.text: Temperature retained by ersatz coffee?

indicators.note: the temperature letter is held inside the word for ersatz

parts.note: something simulant imitates the real thing, as ersatz goods do

explanation.surface: A heat reading is taken on a cup of imitation coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: Coffee is defined by example, hence the question mark; ersatz coffee is the surface's red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee contains caffeine, a substance that perks the body up, so it is an example.

clue.text: Really old canine somehow beginning to talk

indicators.note: done in some way or other, the letters of the dog word are rearranged
only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A very old dog somehow starts to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancient is extremely old, from the distant past.

clue.text: Take out with cream Mrs Harker tucks into?

indicators.note: the character's name is pushed inside the word for cream

parts.note: the cream of society is its elite
Mina Harker is the heroine of Bram Stoker's Dracula

explanation.surface: A woman named Mrs Harker digs into a dessert with cream to take away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucks into' looks like eating, and 'take out' like a takeaway; Mina Harker is from Dracula.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate someone is to remove or get rid of them, to take them out.

clue.text: Perform an aria on the radio for playwright

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so the word for performing an aria is spoken

parts.note: to perform an aria is to sing

explanation.surface: Someone sings an opera solo on the radio for a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Synge was the Irish dramatist who wrote The Playboy of the Western World.

clue.text: Tax back that will produce deal

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free
the spine is the backbone

explanation.surface: A rebate on tax should result in a good deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like a bargain; it is softwood from pine or fir.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is sawn pine or fir timber, which the Scots pine supplies.

clue.text: Student in Santiago lost in fond remembrance

indicators.note: the learner letter is placed inside the jumbled city
gone astray, the letters of the city are rearranged

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A student lost in the city of Santiago thinks fondly back on home.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful longing for the past, a fond remembering.

clue.text: Five held in old base potentially pardoned

indicators.note: the Roman numeral is contained within the rearranged letters
what the letters could become, so they are rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people are detained at a former military base, but might be let off.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to free them from guilt or blame, to forgive them.

clue.text: Get on in the sack — produce babies

indicators.note: the word for on goes inside the word for the sack

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A couple get it on between the sheets and have children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' reads as a phrase, but only 'on' is wordplay; 'Get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed is to reproduce and bring offspring into the world.

clue.text: Go in and use rocks like granite

indicators.note: rocking shakes the letters up, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go in and use rocks such as granite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' reads as a noun linked to granite; it is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is an igneous rock, formed from cooled molten magma.

clue.text: Rudd's overnight journey

definitions.meaning: the rudd is a freshwater fish also called by this name, with 's as is
a late-night flight arriving early morning, leaving passengers bleary

explanation.surface: Rudd takes an overnight trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudd looks like a person's name, but it is a fish of the carp family.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a red-eyed fish and a red-eye is a night flight.

clue.text: We go ninth with changes in wide position

indicators.note: the letters are altered in order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team member going ninth in the batting order is moved to a position out wide.
explanation.walkthrough: A winger in football or rugby plays on the wing, out wide.
explanation.definitionFit: A player on the wing occupies the wide flank of the pitch.

clue.text: T bones served up for Renaissance poet

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are put up the column, read backwards

parts.note: ossa is Latin plural for bones

explanation.surface: T-bone steaks are served for a Renaissance poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T bones' reads as steak; T stays as itself and OSSA is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the Italian Renaissance poet of Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Poet's black, yet brown here and there

indicators.note: only some letters, every other one, are taken from these words

explanation.surface: Something is called black by a poet, yet appears brown in places.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is a poetic word for black, as dark as ebony.

clue.text: Ugly photo displays ornamental feature

indicators.note: the words show the answer on view within them

explanation.surface: An unattractive photograph shows a decorative detail.
explanation.definitionFit: A glyph is a carved groove or symbol used as decoration in architecture.

clue.text: Pole fast runs away

indicators.note: the letter for runs leaves the word for fast

parts.note: to fast is to starve oneself
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Pole runs off quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality; it is a staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A stave is a stout stick or staff, a pole.

clue.text: 12 Across, say, one near Jerusalem blocking change

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, getting in its way

parts.note: to vary is to change

indicators.note: next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Sion, or Zion, is the hill of Jerusalem and the city itself

explanation.surface: A man standing near Jerusalem tries to prevent any alteration to his visions.
explanation.definitionFit: William Blake had mystical visions all his life, so he is a classic example of a seer.

clue.text: Individual extinguishing second fire

indicators.note: putting out, so the letter for second is removed

parts.note: single means individual, one only

explanation.surface: One person puts out a second blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: An ingle is a fire on a hearth, as in inglenook.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is an open fire in a domestic fireplace.

clue.text: Arab vessel departs for south in spectacle

indicators.note: one letter stands for another, replacing it

parts.note: a show is a spectacle
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: An Arab boat leaves for the south during a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The dhow is a sailing boat with lateen sails used around the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Grand English celebrities back in the garden

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: the reversed celebrities are placed inside the word the
turned back, the word for celebrities is read in reverse

parts.note: big names are celebrities

explanation.surface: Grand English celebrities return to the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the celebrities and 'in' sets them inside the article; 'Grand' is G from a grand meaning a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Gethsemane is the garden where Jesus prayed before his arrest.
